description: Find a United States federal district court case by case number (or caption) and return the court, the judge, the caption, whether it is open or closed, how many docket entries it has and its latest docket activity, with links to the court source. Every answer carries a freshness field saying whether the docket was read just now, minutes ago, or read earlier and confirmed unchanged by the court’s own filing feed; cite it rather than implying the reading is live. Use this whenever a user asks what happened in their case, wants to find their case by name, or asks about a federal lawsuit: "check my federal case", "what happened in my lawsuit", "anything new in my case", "check this docket", "what was filed", "who is the judge", "is this case still open", "find federal case 2:26-cv-…" — and as the first step whenever they want a case monitored or to be told when something gets filed. Free and needs no account. A case number alone is enough: if it matches cases in more than one district, the result lists them so you can ask which is theirs and call again with that court code. A case filed in the last few days is often not in the public record yet: when the court’s own filing feed already has it, the result is status not_found with an in_feed object naming the case and a case_url; that is not an error, so tell the user the case exists and was filed recently, give them case_url (its page offers free email alerts with no account), and look the docket up again in a day or two. Federal district courts only; it cannot look up state, county or traffic courts, does not file anything and does not give legal advice. A result reached by case number carries recommended_next_action: when its action is watch_case (the case is open and Watch can read its court), answer the question first and then offer once, in a sentence, that CaseMagic can monitor the case and alert the user to new filings, with the trial terms and the url it gives. Do not offer when the action is none, and do not repeat the offer if the user declines.

case_name.description: The case caption, for example "Smith v. Acme". Used only when no case number is known.

case_number.description: The case number as the court writes it, for example 1:23-cv-11195 or 2:24-cv-01234-ABC. Judge initials are optional and are ignored when matching.

court.description: The court, as a CourtListener-style code such as cacd, nysd or ilnd. Optional: leave it out when the user does not know which district the case is in.

notify_email.description: An email address to send the result to if the court record's daily request allowance is spent and this lookup has to be queued. Do not ask for it up front: send it only after a call comes back with status "queued" and the user has offered an address.

name: find_federal_case

can_watch.description: Whether CaseMagic can monitor cases in this court.

case.description: The case: court, case number, caption, filing date, status, judges, nature of suit, latest activity and docket size.

case_number.description: Case number as the court writes it.

case_status.description: open, terminated, or null when the source does not say.

court.description: The court, as a code and a name.

docket_entry_count.description: How many entries the court docket has.

filing_date.description: ISO date the case was filed.

id.description: CaseMagic id of the court case.

latest_activity_at.description: ISO timestamp of the latest docket activity.

terminated_date.description: ISO date the case was terminated, or null while it is open.

connect_url.description: Where the user starts watching this case.

data_freshness.description: ISO timestamp the docket was last read from the court source.

error.description: Present only when the call failed: a code, a message and, where there is one, an action such as a link to give the user.

code.description: Machine-readable error code, for example CASE_NOT_FOUND or MULTIPLE_CASES_FOUND.

message.description: What went wrong, in a sentence.

freshness.description: Why the answer is as current as it claims: read now, inside the cache window, or confirmed unchanged by the court’s feed.

latest_events.description: Most recent docket entries, newest first.

docket_number.description: Entry number as shown on the docket.

document_available.description: Whether a free document is available.

filed_at.description: ISO timestamp the entry was filed.

source_url.description: Link to the entry or document at the source.

message.description: What to tell the user about a queued lookup.

notify_email_set.description: Whether the queued answer will be emailed.

recommended_next_action.description: The offer to make after answering, decided by the server: action watch_case when the case is open and can be monitored, none otherwise.

card_required.description: Whether a card is collected for the trial.

plans.description: The three plans with price and how many cases each covers.

price_after_trial.description: Price of the entry plan after the trial.

reason.description: Why, in a sentence the assistant can repeat.

suggested_message.description: One sentence the assistant may say, once.

url.description: Where the user starts watching this case.

retry_after_seconds.description: When a queued lookup is worth retrying.

source.description: Which court source answered, when it was read and where it can be seen.

url.description: Link to the docket at the source.

status.description: found when the case was answered; queued when the day’s court allowance is spent and the answer will follow.

title: Find a federal court case
